record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can clean computation, where the evolving memory state reveals no secrets about the computed function at any single time step, be used to obtain a natural class of cryptographic objects, either conditionally or unconditionally?

evidence.quote: In other words, our memory at every point in time reveals no secrets about the computation of f .
Problem 34. Show the existence, conditional or otherwise, of a natural class of cryptographic objects by using clean computation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a deterministic algorithm computing a function f : {0,1}* → {0,1}* a "clean computation" if, at every single time step of its execution, the entire contents of its memory (work tape, registers, and any other internal state) can be simulated efficiently from public information alone, so that the instantaneous memory state at any single time step reveals no secret information about f or its inputs/outputs beyond what is publicly known. (Intuitively, no individual snapshot of the evolving memory leaks any secret, even though the computation as a whole produces a meaningful output.)

Problem: Exhibit a natural class of cryptographic objects — for instance, one-way functions, pseudorandom generators, public-key encryption, digital signatures, or similar primitives — whose existence can be established, either unconditionally or under standard cryptographic assumptions, by means of a clean computation in the above sense. Equivalently, demonstrate that the paradigm of clean computation is powerful enough to yield a natural cryptographic primitive.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a recent survey on techniques for reusing space in computation as an explicitly listed open problem. A targeted web search did not surface any paper announcing the construction of a natural cryptographic primitive from clean computation, suggesting the problem remains open.
